race.name: GFNY Walnut Creek
race.tagline: Sixty-four timed miles, Morgan Territory's technical rollers, and an eleven-mile summit finish on Mount Diablo.

vitals.start_format: Mass-start competitive long course with chip timing
vitals.registration: Online through the official GFNY race site
vitals.feed_zones: Official GFNY aid stations with hydration, food, technical, and medical support
vitals.cutoff_time: See current race guide and official course rules
route_options: Recreational medium route: see official race site

climate.description: April in the East Bay can be cool at the start, warm and exposed inland, and windy near ridges. The summit may be materially colder than Walnut Creek.

terrain.primary: Technical rolling roads into a major summit finish
terrain.surface: Paved East Bay roads, including narrow Morgan Territory Road and the closed Mount Diablo summit road.
features: Steep 10-15% pitches on Morgan Territory Road
A five-mile technical descent from Morgan Territory
An eleven-mile Mount Diablo climb gaining 3,300 feet
A summit timing finish followed by a neutral descent

fondo_rating.scoring_notes: Exceptional climbing density, technical variety, and a true summit finish make this the strongest of GFNY's new California races. First-edition status limits organization and prestige scores.

key_climbs: Steep 10-15% pitches on Morgan Territory Road
A five-mile technical descent from Morgan Territory
An eleven-mile Mount Diablo climb gaining 3,300 feet
A summit timing finish followed by a neutral descent
climb_profile.profile_type: Technical rolling roads into a major summit finish
climb_profile.king_of_mountain: The Mount Diablo summit finish: eleven miles, 3,300 feet of gain, a 5.3 percent average, and a final kicker after the race has already accumulated major climbing.

course_description.character: GFNY Walnut Creek compresses 2,106 meters of climbing into 103.8 timed kilometers. Morgan Territory adds narrow, twisting, steeply pitched roads and a technical descent before the course reaches Mount Diablo for an eleven-mile closed-road summit finish.
course_description.signature_challenge: The Mount Diablo summit finish: eleven miles, 3,300 feet of gain, a 5.3 percent average, and a final kicker after the race has already accumulated major climbing.

logistics.airport: Oakland International Airport (OAK) is the most convenient major airport; San Francisco (SFO) also works with more traffic exposure.
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Walnut Creek near Shadelands or downtown. Confirm early bike storage and transport because the race finishes on Mount Diablo before a neutral return.
logistics.transport: Use official race-week instructions for packet pickup, start access, and bike transport.
logistics.food: Walnut Creek has extensive dining and grocery options. The race's steep climbing rewards a light familiar breakfast and aggressive fueling from the start.

history.origin_story: GFNY announced Walnut Creek in May 2026 around an unusual race design: a technical East Bay loop followed by a timed summit finish on Mount Diablo.
history.reputation: An unproven first edition with a course credible enough to become a destination race if operations match the design.

biased_opinion.summary: GFNY Walnut Creek compresses 2,106 meters of climbing into 103.8 timed kilometers. Morgan Territory adds narrow, twisting, steeply pitched roads and a technical descent before the course reaches Mount Diablo for an eleven-mile closed-road summit finish.
weaknesses: A strict Mount Diablo cutoff can end the competitive route
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A short-by-distance but major-by-elevation race that demands climbing power, descending judgment, and cutoff-aware pacing.

final_verdict.one_liner: Sixty-four timed miles, Morgan Territory's technical rollers, and an eleven-mile summit finish on Mount Diablo.
final_verdict.should_you_race: A short-by-distance but major-by-elevation race that demands climbing power, descending judgment, and cutoff-aware pacing.
final_verdict.alternatives: GFNY Ventura for a longer loop, or the established Levi's GranFondo Growler for a much longer Northern California test.
